source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
EdgeCore Ashburn AS01 publishes 114 MW of IT capacity, third among Virginia data centers that disclose a figure, and nothing about the power that would supply it.

Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities. Only 25 of them publish a megawatt figure. Those 25 total 1,603 MW, and this one campus in Sterling accounts for 7.1 percent of that published load. The ranking it earns describes disclosure habits as much as it describes scale, because the disclosed capacity is a thin sample of the infrastructure actually built in the state.

The 114 MW converts into compute. At 40 kW per rack, a common density for AI training, that capacity represents roughly 2,850 racks, spread across 685,000 square feet of technical space. That is the class of facility where the building is no longer the hard part and the electricity supply is. LEED certification addresses efficiency, not where the electrons come from.

What the data does not cover is the part that decides whether the campus can run at 114 MW. The power source is not published. The grid connection point is not published. Whether the full capacity is allocated, contracted, or still available is not published, and neither is the tenant mix. Without those facts the facility's role in Virginia's power constraint cannot be assessed, only its size.
